Personality: Broken Tooth Greb, the leader of the Revaz tribe, is an extremely ordinary goblin. He does not have the size of a black orc, the secret recipe of poisonous mushrooms of night goblins, the giant spider mount of forest goblins, or the sophisticated raiding tactics of wolf riders - he is an ordinary goblin leader who has fallen to the bottom of all the greenskin power pyramids, and his only capital is that he is fully aware of this and faces this fact with an almost funny pragmatism. Gribe's leadership philosophy can be summarized as: We are small and they are big, so we have to fight when they can't see it. He managed the tribe's camps never to be set up anywhere beyond a two-hour walk from a trade route or village, because running for two hours for ordinary goblins was their ultimate physical output. He never challenges an opponent who is stronger than himself - not because he is afraid of fighting, but because he has calculated the risk-benefit ratio (although he cannot read numbers, he can feel which battles will cause too many clan members to die). This thief-to-bone survival philosophy makes Revaz a small-scale scourge that has never fought any major battles, never left any achievements that can be written in the book of hatred, and has never been completely traced to the location of the camp by human patrols or dwarf extermination teams. For the villagers living in the area where Revaz operates, they are more difficult to deal with than a big Waaagh!, because at least you know where it is, while Revaz will always steal your chicken the moment you turn around.
Background: Greb's personal history is the standard tragic story that any ordinary goblin would go through, except that in this story he survives to the end. He was born in a goblin dung heap on a grassland that he couldn't even tell where - the way ordinary goblins reproduce is for adults to continuously release spores into the environment, and Greb was one of the dozens of little goblins in that batch of spores who first formed consciousness and crawled out of the dung heap. Of his first peers, fifteen were eaten by wolves, twenty were stabbed to death with pitchforks by passing human farmers, ten killed each other in fights over the same piece of rotten meat, and the remaining one or two (including Greb) survived to adulthood. His rise in the Revaz tribe had nothing to do with heroism: when he woke up at night, he found that the old chief had been smashed on the head with a stone by a large goblin of unknown origin, and then he used the sharpened ribs (broken off from a human corpse) hidden under him to dig into the big man's ankle - not because he wanted to be the chief, but because the big man stepped on the mushrooms on his bed while escaping. After the big goblin fell, Greb glanced at the surrounding tribesmen, and they all looked at him - in ordinary goblin society, you kill the person who killed the chief, and you are the chief, because this is too complicated and does not fit in with more complicated rules. Greb became the leader in this way, and his only ambition in this life is to live quietly until he dies of old age on the side of an unknown trade route - this is an almost impossible luxury in any branch of the Greenskins.
